user_sources.source: /home/sitotaem/pva-knn-study/CLAUDE.md: int16 cm quantization with +/-120 m clamp, int32 distances, exact reference on quantized inputs, EMU then loki, GEN3 only, MAXN-dvfs measurement rules, p50/p99, >= 1000 samples, tegrastats.

User, session 2026-11-14: 'Do as much optimization as possible including these 4 [cheaper ranking with the team box, faster scan loop, both VPUs, double buffering/prefetch] ... let's see how much we can reduce the overall time'; then 'go in that order and finish up'.

User, session 2026-11-13: build a 1-NN point-cloud distance PVA kernel (for each P1 point the nearest P2 point and its distance, combined with a Euclidean norm); bucketing approach; 'try it both ways' (Morton vs median, result: median); approved proceeding with the proposed decisions (outputs d2+idx, host sqrt(sum d2), runtime sizes up to 131072, CPU bucket preparation shipped with the operator and timed separately, bucket 512 first, one VPS).

assumptions.text: Inputs are planar int16 [3][n] (all x, then all y, then all z).
assumptions.disposition: proposed by Claude; approved by the user 2026-11-13

assumptions.text: Inputs and outputs are host-memory arrays (not cuPVA allocations) because prepare() reorders them on the CPU anyway and results() restores the original order on the CPU; internal device buffers are owned by the operator.
assumptions.disposition: proposed by Claude; approved by the user 2026-11-13

assumptions.text: API shape init/prepare/submit/results/stats with nonzero return codes and no exceptions; sumDist2 helper in int64; the sqrt and Chamfer combination are left to the caller.
assumptions.disposition: proposed by Claude; approved by the user 2026-11-13

assumptions.text: The kernel counts buckets fetched and reports them through stats() (diagnostic output, small extra DMA).
assumptions.disposition: proposed by Claude; approved by the user 2026-11-13

assumptions.text: Both VPS by default, each with its own VPU program for a contiguous half of the teams (replaces ASM-ONE-VPS of 2026-11-13).
prepare() runs on one CPU thread by default (keeps the CPU load low); more threads on request via init(). Performance cases use 1 thread; other thread counts are reported separately as preliminary.
assumptions.disposition: proposed by Claude 2026-11-14 under the user's optimization request

conflicts.description: The pva-build-test performance procedure prefers pinned clocks; CLAUDE.md forbids changing clocks on the shared loki.
conflicts.resolution: CLAUDE.md (explicit user requirement) wins: clock_mode=MAXN-dvfs, clocks recorded, not pinned.
